analysis:
Only docs/reference/configuration.md was supplied: base lines 309-571 and head lines 1-308. No patch hunks or diff were visible, so the exact before/after delta could not be compared. No code is changed, and I found no security regression in the visible text.

Visible head content touching the threat model:
- Head 127-143 documents DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION as exact `1`, internal-only and not production-ready. It is the only App Attest flag forwarded to the LaunchAgent (LaunchAgent.swift passthroughEnvironment). Native diagnostic and fault-injection flags are not forwarded. Worker failures do not fall back to in-process Apple calls. This matches TB-011 (default-off candidate) and T-053/T-057.
- Head 67-88 documents endpoint resumption and logout. Protocol 1 uses a fixed process key and a fresh nonce per socket. `logout --config` cannot retarget revocation; revocation uses issuer metadata bound to the saved token. Missing metadata means local-only logout. This is consistent with A-008 and T-053.
- Base 473-504 describes the SSD prefix cache and matches T-041: TTL capped at 1800 s, environment can only shorten it, and the disk budget is half of available space with a 20 GiB fallback. cache.directory and cache.volume_uuid describe the CacheVolume/CacheStorage UUID pinning. The documented 20 GiB free-space write reserve is also consistent.
- Base 492-498 keeps DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL, TEST_ROOT and TEST_PERSISTENT_KEY off by default and not forwarded to LaunchAgents (the persistent-key flag explicitly). Cross-check that code does not forward them.
- The EnvironmentScrubber DYLD/LD_PRELOAD list (base 556) is unchanged in kind (T-014/T-013).

Coverage limit: code behavior was not reviewed. Later passes should verify that the code in the cited files (LaunchAgent.swift, SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift, CacheStorage.swift, LogoutCommand.swift) matches these claims.
